Generation bands are computed by the API with this recursive CTE (roots = couples where neither partner appears in child_of as a child):
WITH RECURSIVE bands AS (SELECT c.couple_id, c.tree_id, 1 AS gen FROM couple c WHERE c.tree_id = :tree AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM child_of co WHERE co.child_person_id = c.partner_a OR co.child_person_id = c.partner_b) UNION ALL SELECT kc.couple_id, b.tree_id, b.gen + 1 FROM bands b JOIN child_of co ON co.couple_id = b.couple_id JOIN couple kc ON kc.partner_a = co.child_person_id OR kc.partner_b = co.child_person_id)

Done — `pnpm exec vitest run test/schema.test.ts` is green (10/10 passing), and `pnpm typecheck` is clean. Only in-scope files were written: `migrations/0001_init.sql`, `migrations/0002_seed.sql`, `test/schema.test.ts`.

What the suite proves:
- CHECK constraints: `tree_access.role='admin'` and `person.gender='x'` both rejected.
- FK enforcement: with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, an orphan `child_of` insert fails.
- Recursive CTE (verbatim from spec): Narayanan tree yields bands 1..4 with exactly one couple per band and child_count 1 on the g4 couple; Path tree yields bands 1..2.
- PK uniqueness: duplicate `(lang, relation_key)` into `kin_term` fails.
- Seed shape: all three indexes exist, every language has all canonical keys, and Aadhira/Srijan exist as unmarried children of their respective g4/g2 couples.

Two judgment calls worth knowing about:
1. The authoritative row list contains no `self` row even though `self` is a canonical key. I treated `self` as runtime-only (identity resolution lives in TypeScript) and documented that in the test rather than inventing unlisted seed rows.
2. The sheet lists `bn|ma|ma|mother`; `ma` isn't a canonical relation key, so it's stored as `bn|mo|ma|mother` (term/gloss verbatim) — noted in the seed header comment.

Red-first was followed: initial run failed with ENOENT on `0001_init.sql`, then SQL was written until green. No commit made, per instructions.
